title: Stability Guard Rotation and Hotfix Timeline
content:
Meeting: Stability Guard Rotation / Hotfix Triage
Date: 2024-11-04 09:30 PT
Location: Zoom + #release-ops (thread pinned)
Facilitator: Marion Lopez
Attendees: Marion Lopez (owner), Evan Chen (serving-runtime), Priya Narang (SRE), Tobias Müller (release-eng), Samir Gupta (platform), oncall: Jia Park

Purpose
- Weekly stability-guard rotation: consolidate hotfix candidates, verify rollback readiness, and signoff short windows for upcoming release trains.
- Make a quick go/no-go on two queued hotfixes and agree on canary ramp plans for next week.

Agenda
1) Quick state (rollouts, metrics) — 09:30–09:38
2) Hotfix triage — HF-337 (latency spike), HF-338 (canary regression) — 09:38–09:55
3) Change window approvals & contingency playbooks — 09:55–10:10
4) Action items & owners — 10:10–10:20
5) AOB / Notes to self — 10:20–10:25

1) Quick state
- Current release train: v1.28.3 (canary 25% in us-west2) — health: degraded p95 on generation endpoint (serving-runtime).
- SLOs: 99th percentile latency target 600ms; observed p95 ~1.35s in the last 6h on canary.
- Error budget: ~0.7% remaining for the week for generation route.
- Recent deploys: runtime PR #1142 (kv-cache backpressure change) merged 2024-11-03 and rolled to canary 2h after merge.

2) Hotfix triage (decision summary first)
HOTFIX HF-337: serving-runtime p95 spike after kv-cache change
- Symptoms: sudden p95 increase (x2), tail latency spikes correlated with long KV cache miss events. No user-visible 5xx increase yet.
- First detection: alert from synthetic-checks at 02:17 UTC; oncall paged at 02:21 UTC.
- Root hypothesis: PR #1142 introduced subtle lock contention under particular request interleavings at seq_len > 1024.
- Tests run: local repro by Evan (ramp generator with seq_len 1200) reproduced ~40% of spike.
- Risk: High for large-context workloads; medium for typical 256-token flows.
- Proposed mitigations (short-term):
  * Immediate: throttle new canary traffic to 10% and disable long-seq routing to canary (Priya) — ACTION: Priya to apply traffic-split by 09:45 PT.
  * Quick rollback plan: Fast rollback to runtime v1.28.2 build from artifact store; rollback script already validated in canary last month. Tobias to be on-call for rollback window (10m).
  * Hotfix patch: revert kv-lock change + add fine-grained instrumentation + unit test for interleavings — Evan to open HF branch and PR.
- Decision: Apply traffic-throttle to 10% (approved). If p95 does not reduce to <800ms in 30m, rollback to v1.28.2 (pre-approved).
- Tickets: RINF-1823 (primary), follow-up RINF-1827 (tests & metrics).

HOTFIX HF-338: canary regression in batching logic (minor loss of throughput)
- Symptoms: Canary shows 6% throughput drop at high concurrent qps (observed in load test, not production).
- Cause: batching window tuning change that increases micro-batching under certain seq distribution.
- Risk: Low-to-medium; regression reduces efficiency but not correctness.
- Proposed approach: Delay full rollout, add metric patch to surface batching ratio, continue monitoring at 10% canary for 24h. If no further regressions, proceed with staged ramp.
- Decision: Hold HF-338 as "monitor and instrument" — no immediate rollback. Evan to add batching metrics PR by EOD.

3) Change window approvals & contingency playbooks
- Next major window: 2024-11-07 02:00–05:00 UTC (canary ramp to 50% -> 100% if green).
- Preflight checklist items (owners):
  * Canary health synthetic run (smoke + long-seq) — Samir (to run 2h pre-window)
  * Rollback artifact validation (checksum & compatibility test) — Tobias
  * DB connection pool tunables review — Priya
  * Customer notification list (if rollout > 30% affects SLA) — CS ops (Samir to coordinate)
- Contingency policy (agreed):
  * On p95 > 900ms for >15m: immediate 20% rollback -> Observe 10m. If persists, full rollback.
  * On error-rate increase >0.5% above baseline: immediate pause and triage.
  * On storage pressure or OOM events: immediate full rollback and incident bridge.
- Short scripts to run (handbook):
  * rollback-to-1.28.2.sh (tested) — location: s3://redwood-deploy/artifacts/rollbacks/1.28.2/rollback-to-1.28.2.sh
  * canary-traffic-shift.sh — automates traffic-splitting via typeless route config.
  * snapshot-kv-cache.sh — create KV cache snapshot for debugging.

4) Action items (owners + due dates)
- Priya: apply canary throttle to 10% and remove long-seq routing to canary — due 2024-11-04 09:45 PT — status: in_progress.
- Evan: open HF branch to revert kv-lock change + create reproducible test harness (RINF-1827) — due 2024-11-05 EOD — status: assigned.
- Tobias: validate rollback artifacts and rehearse rollback steps with Samir — due 2024-11-04 12:00 PT — status: assigned.
- Samir: run extended synthetic suite 2h before next change window (incl. long-seq) and post results to #release-ops — due 2024-11-06 23:00 UTC — status: assigned.
- Jia Park (oncall): monitor #synth-health and escalate to bridge if alerts >3 within 30m — ongoing.

5) Notes / Observations / To-do list (informal)
- Notes to self: we keep hitting edge cases around seq_len distribution — need a dedicated regression suite with randomized interleavings covering kv-cache hot paths. Add to backlog under eng/served-tests.
- Question: can we add a heuristic in the router to avoid sending seq_len > 1024 to experimental canaries? Pros/cons discussed: safer but masks bugs. Action: document the tradeoff and bring to architecture sync (Evan + Priya).
- Suggestion: label canary runs with workload signatures so postmortems can filter by seq distribution. (Samir)

Triage timeline (short log)
- 02:17 UTC: synthetic alert (p95 spike)
- 02:21 UTC: oncall page -> Jia Park acknowledges
- 02:40 UTC: initial rollback considered, but Evan reproduces locally; patch planned
- 03:15 UTC: decision to throttle canary (10%) and instrument more metrics
- 09:30 UTC: stability-guard meeting confirms traffic throttle and rollback pre-approval

Follow-ups for next rotation (2024-11-11)
- Confirm HF-337 patch test coverage and integration results (Evan).
- Evaluate the effect of canary throttle on customer-facing latencies (Priya + Samir).
- Draft short how-to for rollback-runbook for new SRE hires (Tobias).

Appendix: quick references
- Repro commands (internal):
  * python infra/tools/ramp_generator.py --seq_len 1200 --qps 300 --duration 1200s --target runtime-canary
  * curl -H 'x-workload-signature: longseq' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/gen/test-synth
- Helpful searches:
  * Logs: "kv-cache miss" tag in Loki, timeframe 2024-11-04 00:00–06:00 UTC
  * Dashboards: generation-route > latency > p95 (canary overlay)

End notes
- Tone: keep this doc as the short-lived operational ledger for the active window. Move final postmortem + RCA to Confluence if we execute a rollback or ship hotfix.
- Next guard rotation: 2024-11-11 09:30 PT.

-- Marion (notes)

Unresolved/parking lot (for architecture sync):
- Evaluate whether batching heuristics should be per-customer (tenant-aware) vs. global to avoid performance cliffs.
- Decide on policy for masking canary traffic by seq length: temporary mitigation vs permanent router rule.

Slack threads / immediate links

- Pager duty incident (if escalated): PD-INC-4932
